title.narrative: Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Solomon Islands

description.narrative: The objective of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program Project for the Federated States of Micronesia is to strengthen the shared management of selected Pacific Island oceanic and coastal fisheries, and the critical habitats upon which they depend. The project has four components. (1) Sustainable management of oceanic fisheries component will help participating Pacific Island countries strengthen the management of the region's purse seine and long-line tuna fisheries. The component includes activities to: (i) strengthen the capacity of national and regional institutions to sustainably manage Pacific Island tuna fisheries; and (ii) ensure an equitable distribution within Pacific Island countries of the benefits of sustainably managed tuna fisheries. (2) Sustainable management of coastal fisheries component aims to support participating countries to sustainably manage defined coastal fisheries and the habitats that support them, focusing on those with the greatest potential for increased benefits, i.e. coastal fisheries such as beche-de-mer (BDM) that (i) can generate export earnings for the country, and/or (ii) support livelihoods, food security and dietary health. Towards this objective, this component includes activities to: (i) empower stakeholders to sustainably manage targeted coastal fisheries in participating countries; and (ii) link sustainable coastal fish products to regional markets. This component will provide climate change co-benefits by supporting adaptation in the form of better management of coastal fisheries and natural defenses. (3) Sustainable financing of the conservation of critical fishery habitats component will help identify revenue streams to sustainably finance the conservation of critical habitats that underpin oceanic and coastal fisheries in the region. This component also provides climate change co-benefits by supporting mitigation, in the form of conservation of vegetated coastal habitats that sequester significant amounts of carbon. (4) Regional coordination, implementation support, national program management and monitoring and evaluation component will provide regional coordination, implementation support and project management, to ensure a coherent approach to program implementation and wide dissemination of results and lessons learned; as well as implementation support and training as needed for the program to achieve its objectives.
The objective of the Project is to strengthen the shared management of selected Pacific Island oceanic and coastal fisheries, and the critical habitats upon which they depend.

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits that are addressed
MFMRs monitoring, control and surveillance institutional capacity strengthened through expansion of the Compliance Officer Program

comment.narrative: <p>10 of the 24 certified compliance officers are female (42%). Over time, these Compliance Officers have been absorbed in to the public service staff establishment and at project closure only two were still funded by PROP and were planned for absorption into MFMR after project closure. One officer left MFMR so the number reduced from 25 to 24 in the reporting period. </p>

title.narrative: Coastal fish resources assessed as the basis for improved management

comment.narrative: <p>Assessments for coral, clams and trochus were completed.</p>

title.narrative: Management plans for key coastal fish species implemented in the Solomon Islands

comment.narrative: <p>Three management plans are under implementation: coral, trochus and giant clam (clam and corals are addressed in a single shared document).  The beche-de-mer plan was also updated.</p>

title.narrative: Coastal fisheries management plans designed for key species in the Solomon Islands

comment.narrative: <p>Three management plans were prepared and are under implementation: coral, trochus and giant clam.  An existing beche-de-mer plan was also updated.</p>

title.narrative: Electronic monitoring system for long-line vessels piloted in the Solomon Islands

comment.narrative: <p>EMS has been successfully piloted in seven long-line vessels. The system was rolled out to an additional nine vessels prior to project closure.</p>

title.narrative: Electronic Monitoring System for long-line vessels developed in the Solomon Islands

comment.narrative: <p>Electronic monitoring system for long-line vessels has been developed in the Solomon Islands as a part of the pilot program. It was rolled out to an additional 9 vessels during the remaining life of the project.</p>
